summary:
Little Oppy ! is an interactive, gamified web odyssey that brings NASA’s dormant Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity (MER-B) back to life for the Artemis Generation. Sourced directly from authentic NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) archives, JPL Photojournal records, and MRO Context Camera (CTX) mosaics, the project transforms Opportunity from discarded space hardware into an active, emotional STEM learning monument.

Students inspect Opportunity's hardware in full 3D WebGL, relive the historic 2004 airbag landing, and pilot the rover across a physics-driven 2D Martian regolith engine. Along her 45.16 km traverse from Eagle Crater to Endeavour Crater, students uncover 6 verified planetary science milestones narrated through synchronized original voice acting. The experience culminates in an emotional Sol 5,111 tribute to Opportunity’s final transmission during the global dust storm of 2018. Built with a zero-dependency architecture, Little Oppy ! loads instantly on any school Chromebook, tablet, or smartphone without installation.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO & HOW DOES IT WORK?

Little Oppy ! is a multi-stage educational web simulation that tells the 15-year survival story of NASA's Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity (2004–2018). It is structured into 6 progressive stages:

1. Interactive 3D Rover Hardware: Rotate, inspect, and explore the Pancam mast, solar arrays, and alpha-particle X-ray spectrometer in full WebGL.

2. Launch & Airbag Touchdown: Relive the January 2004 bouncing airbag landing at Eagle Crater with authentic telemetry archives.

3. Authentic MRO CTX Orbital Map: A high-resolution cartographic route map built from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Context Camera imagery displaying all 6 milestone waypoints across her 45.16 km traverse.

4. 2D Regolith Expedition Game: A custom 60 FPS HTML5 Canvas game engine where players pilot Opportunity across Martian sand dunes, managing wheel traction, slope elevation, and dynamic dust devils.

5. Interactive Science Milestones: Progressive scientific discovery modals where Opportunity narrates her findings in synchronization with real-time typewriter subtitles and NASA JPL imagery.

6. Sol 5,111 Grand Finale: An emotional simulation of the catastrophic 2018 global dust storm at Perseverance Valley, cutting to authentic static telemetry before Opportunity delivers her final farewell message.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT:

• Active Agency Over Passive Reading: Students earn scientific facts through driving rather than memorizing dry textbook pages.

• Mechanical STEM Role Model: Illustrates perseverance and engineering triumph—overcoming stuck wheels, sand traps in Purgatory Dune, and failing flash memory.

• Accessible Worldwide: Built with a lightweight, zero-dependency architecture that runs instantly in any browser without multi-gigabyte downloads or specialized gaming hardware.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & HARDWARE:

• Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, ES6+ Vanilla JavaScript

• 3D Rendering: WebGL & Google Model-Viewer

• Game Physics: HTML5 2D Canvas with kinematics, traction damping, and sinusoidal terrain slope curves

• Audio Engine: Web Audio API procedural synthesis (Maxon DC motor hum, typewriter clicks, and TV static crash noise)

• Voice Narration: Custom voice acting synchronized with typewriter subtitles across 7 master audio tracks

• Hosting: Global Anycast Edge CDN on Netlify with byte-range HTTP streaming

CREATIVITY & FACTORS CONSIDERED:

Rather than treating Opportunity as discarded "space debris," our project personifies her as an enduring monument to human curiosity. By giving her an authentic voice and coupling genuine NASA planetary photography with accessible retro-futuristic arcade aesthetics, we bridge the gap between retired hardware and the next generation of lunar and Martian explorers.
